description: Right to fix / loss of mechanical knowledge — essay-derived pairs. Thesis novel/asserted; Honda Cub used as illustrative corpus-vs-material knowledge example, not a measured failure rate.

pairs.source_text: What is the core question of Right to Fix and the Loss of Mechanical Knowledge?
pairs.target_text: What is lost when ordinary people can no longer inspect, disassemble, reassemble, and verify the machines and intelligent systems they depend on — and when AI fluent explanation is mistaken for the same thing as material understanding?

pairs.source_text: What learning loop does the right-to-fix essay treat as the spine of repair literacy?
pairs.target_text: Take the system apart far enough to see components and dependencies; observe fit, sequence, wear, and failure; reassemble into a working whole; build a mental model for diagnosis; consult external documentation only where the object cannot safely teach the rest (torque, clearance, model-year procedure).

pairs.source_text: Why does the essay open with a Honda Cub chatbot example?
pairs.target_text: The Cub is one of the most-documented vehicles in history, so a chatbot will likely get the general ignition architecture right and still get a model-year specific wrong — and in repair one wrong thing is not trivia. It separates corpus knowledge from material/variant knowledge.
pairs.reason: DRAFT opening; illustrative, not a measured error rate

pairs.source_text: What shifts does the essay say eroded conditions for learning by disassembly?
pairs.target_text: Sealed modules and proprietary fasteners; lost or paywalled manuals; dealer-only diagnostics and software pairing; disposable design; cultural devaluation of repair labor; platform/subscription dependence that makes ownership conditional.

pairs.source_text: How does the essay widen right-to-repair beyond consumer slogans?
pairs.target_text: As a learning and labor issue: parts, manuals, tools, software access, modifiability, disassembly as teaching, and skilled labor that can still transmit the method. Understanding and repair are one loop.

pairs.source_text: How does the essay connect right-to-fix to local-first AI?
pairs.target_text: AI enclosure can hide the same loss of inspectability: fluent answers without open weights, local tools, or verifiable chains. Local-first stacks are framed as preserving the disassembly loop for intelligent systems — not as nostalgia for old machines.
pairs.reason: README AI enclosure + portfolio link to sovereign AI

pairs.source_text: What are the claim boundaries for the right-to-fix research packet?
pairs.target_text: Design/essay research on repair literacy and inspectability. Not a claim that old machines were simply better, not a rollback program, not a peer-reviewed labor-economics result. Honda Cub example is illustrative. Policy right-to-repair statutes exist in multiple jurisdictions — cite specific bills/laws when making legal claims; this packet is about epistemology and autonomy.
